title: Webhooks > Managing Webhooks > Creating, Updating, and Deleting Webhooks
text:
Webhooks can be managed within the application UI under: **System Tools > Integration > Webhook Subscriptions.**

* * *

title: Webhooks > Designing for Webhooks > Key Considerations:
text:
1.  **Message Order**: Webhooks are not guaranteed to be delivered in chronological order. For example, an "Object Created" webhook might fail and retry later than an "Object Updated" webhook.
    -   **Best Practice**: Use the REST API to retrieve real-time data when processing webhook messages.
2.  **Response Time**: If the webhook publisher does not receive a `200 OK` response within 30 seconds, it will assume failure and enqueue a retry.
    -   **Recommendation**: Respond immediately to webhook callouts and perform additional processing asynchronously.
3.  **Irrelevant Responses**: Avoid returning status responses from unrelated REST API calls, as they are not relevant to webhook operation.

* * *

title: Webhooks > Integration Callouts in Workflows
text: Integration Callouts are a type of webhook that fires when a task reaches a specific status within a workflow (e.g., "In Progress"). These are also known as **Task Status Action Webhooks** (`CalloutLocation: 100`).

title: Webhooks > Integration Callouts in Workflows > Setup Steps:
text:
1.  Navigate to **System Administration > Integration > Webhook Subscriptions**.
2.  Select **Task Status Action** for the "WebHook Source Location."
3.  Assign a **Title**, which will appear under the workflow's Integration Callout section as a selectable option.
4.  Attach the webhook to specific workflow events.
5.  Note: It may take up to 15 minutes for the webhook subscription to become fully active.

* * *

title: Webhooks > mTLS Security in Webhooks
text: Aprimo Productivity Management supports optional **mTLS authentication** for webhooks.

title: Webhooks > mTLS Security in Webhooks > Key Features:
text:
-   A global certificate is used to sign requests to verify they originate from Aprimo.
-   You can validate the certificate using Aprimo’s public key certificate.

title: Webhooks > mTLS Security in Webhooks > Steps to Enable mTLS:
text:
1.  Obtain Aprimo’s public key certificate by contacting your Aprimo representative.
2.  Enable the **Send mTLS Certificate With WebHooks** system parameter:
    -   Go to **Administration > Configuration > System Parameters > System > Security**.
3.  Note: Changes may take up to 15 minutes to take effect.

title: Introducing Webhooks: Automate Processes with Event-Driven Actions
text:
Webhooks are a powerful feature that enable automated, event-driven interactions both within your application and with external systems. By defining specific conditions, you can configure webhooks to trigger processes—whether they occur inside the application or involve external services—when those conditions are met. This allows you to create seamless workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and extend the functionality of your application.

When a webhook is triggered, it can execute actions such as sending an HTTPS call with contextual information to an external service or initiating internal processes within the application. This flexibility ensures webhooks can be tailored to a wide range of integration and automation needs.

title: Introducing Webhooks: Automate Processes with Event-Driven Actions > Key Features of Webhooks:
text:
-   **Event-Driven Triggers**: Define conditions that automatically trigger processes when met.
-   **Versatile Action Options**: Use webhooks to initiate internal application processes or connect with external systems.
-   **Customizable Workflows**: Configure the data, actions, and conditions to fit your specific business logic.
-   **Flexible Execution**: Trigger actions on object creation, updates, deletions, or at specific points in a workflow.

Webhooks provide a dynamic and efficient way to automate processes, enabling users to streamline operations, integrate with external systems, and drive productivity both within and beyond the application.

title: DAM API: GET /accesslist/{accessListId} > GET /api/core/accesslist/{accessListId} > Parameters
text:
- `accessListId` (path, required): id of the access list
- `API-VERSION` (header, required): The REST API version to target, e.g. "1".
- `Accept` (header, required): The desired response media type. If omitted, the server defaults to "application/hal+json", which includes "_links"/"_embedded" hypermedia so a client can navigate to related resources without constructing URLs itself. For most integrations, requesting "application/json" instead is simpler and produces a smaller, flatter response - recommended unless you need that hypermedia.
- `Authorization` (header, required): The bearer token used to authenticate the request.
- `User-Agent` (header, required): Identifies the calling application.

title: DAM API: GET /checks/{checkId}/checkresults > GET /api/core/checks/{checkId}/checkresults
text:
Reads a page of the check results of one check across content item file versions, each with its findings and the feedback recorded on them

Reads a page of the check results of one check across content item file versions, each with its findings and the feedback recorded on them. Use page and pageSize, or skip and take (at most 100 check results per page; larger values are reduced to 100), and read totalCount in the response to determine whether more pages remain. Findings with no feedback are included; feedback is omitted on those findings. Claims Matching returns an empty list. Only check results on content the user can read are returned and counted.

title: DAM API: GET /checks/{checkId}/checkresults > GET /api/core/checks/{checkId}/checkresults > Examples
text:
Reading the check results of one check, with their findings and the feedback recorded on them

Returns a page of the check results of that check across content item file versions. Findings are always included, with the feedback recorded on each finding; findings without feedback are included and omit the feedback field. A positive rating has no reasonCode. A negative rating includes the reasonCode, which the finding feedback reasons list resolves to a title. Use the page and pageSize query parameters, or skip and take, and read totalCount in the response, the number of check results of the check, to determine whether more pages remain. Claims Matching returns an empty list. Only check results on content the user can read are returned and counted. The additionalData of the findings is never returned.

```http
GET /checks/4f6a1c2e8b904d119a221c3d5e7f90ab/checkresults
accept: application/hal+json
```

title: DAM API: PUT /classification/{classificationId} > PUT /api/core/classification/{classificationId} > Examples
text:
Immediate propagation for classification updates.

For POST, PUT and DELETE operations on the /classification resource you can force an immediate update of the search index, or immediate propagation. To do so, add the boolean header/query-string parameter **set-immediateSearchIndexUpdate** and set it to "true". If you don't specify this parameter, or set it to "false", the change will be added to the queue of the Enterprise search synchronization process. Setting the parameter to true will immediately push the classification changes to the search index, so that this classification can immediately be found, e.g. while an ETL import is still running. This is important, for example, when importing both the child and parent classifications.

text:

The available options for fileMode are "UploadFile", "NoFile", "CreateFromUrl" and "CreateFromSmartAgent". The default option is "UploadFile". If fileMode is set to either "NoFile", "CreateFromUrl" or "CreateFromSmartAgent", defaultFileExtensions cannot be used. The titleConfiguration must also always use the option "Field". If the fileMode is not "CreateFromUrl" or "CreateFromSmartAgent", fileConfiguration can be null.
- For fileConfiguration, crawlLevelOption can be either "Fixed" or "Field"
- If crawlLevelOption is "Fixed", the crawlLevelValue field must be used and the crawlLevelFieldId field must not be used.
- If crawlLevelOption is "Field", the crawlLevelFieldId field must be used and the crawlLevelValue field must not be used.

title: DAM API: GET /downloadlink/{downloadLinkId} > GET /api/core/downloadlink/{downloadLinkId} > Examples
text:
Reading a download link without embedded targets

In case of **hal+json**, all subresources (targets) are represented as links to these resources.

In case of **json**, all subresources (targets) are returned as null values.

See the `Reading a download link without embedded targets (hal+json)` and `Reading a download link without embedded targets (json)` response examples in the responses panel.

```http
GET /downloadlink/b6d2400e-ffce-489b-9e08-7324c9378206
accept: application/hal+json
```

```http
GET /downloadlink/b6d2400e-ffce-489b-9e08-7324c9378206
accept: application/json
```

Reading a download link with embedded targets

Read a download link and embed targets.

```http
GET /downloadlink/e8a98a7a0ac1440ba538ad44011948d5
accept: application/hal+json
select-downloadlink: targets
```

text:
Uploading a file

See the Uploading files overview section for details.

Adding or updating a record's file

After a file upload process is finished, you will receive a file upload token. You can use this token to add or update a record's files or file versions. See the examples on creating a record (POST /records) and editing a record (PUT /record/{recordId}) for more details on how to do it. Keep in mind, the file upload token can be consumed only once. **404 Not Found** error response is returned if you try consuming a token more than once.

Applying a watermark to a file

Configured through the creation of a record (POST /records) and/or editing of a record (PUT /record/{recordId}). For more info, see the Watermark resource page.

title: DAM API: GET /filepreview/{filePreviewId} > GET /api/core/filepreview/{filePreviewId} > Examples
text:
Uploading a file preview

See the Uploading files overview section for details.

Adding or updating a file preview

After a file preview upload process is finished, you will receive a file upload token. You can use this token to add or update a file preview. See the examples on creating a record (POST /records) and editing a record (PUT /record/{recordId}) for more details on how to do it. Keep in mind, the file upload token can be consumed only once. **404 Not Found** error response is returned if you try consuming that token more than once.

When adding a file version of a supported format, a preview can be generated automatically. If you want to edit the metadata of this automatically generated preview in the same request you send to create the version, you can do this by specifying the same file upload token used to add the file version as id of the preview. This will not be considered consuming the token, but is only used as convention to address the autogenerated file preview.

text:
- `id`: Identifier for this check result.
- `fileVersionId`: File version identifier for this check result.
- `checkId`: Check identifier for this check result.
- `description`: Summary the user sees first, e.g. "Three issues were found". Best practice: immediately after starting an external check, create a result with outcome "info" and a description like "In Progress" so the user knows the request was received; when the check completes, PUT that same result with the final outcome and description, rather than creating a new one.

If left unset, it is derived from this result's findings: 0 findings -> no badge shown; 1+ fail -> red badge (count of fail+warn); 1+ warn, 0 fail -> orange badge (count of warnings); 1+ pass, 0 fail/warn -> green badge (count of passes); 1+ info, 0 fail/warn/pass -> gray "Info" badge. Setting outcome explicitly overrides this rollup.
- `createdById`: ID of the user who created this check result.
- `createdOn`: Creation datetime in UTC time.
- `_links`: Hypermedia links (HAL-style) to related resources.
- `_embedded`: Hypermedia-embedded (HAL-style) related resources, inlined here when requested/expanded.

title: DAM API: GET /fileversion/{fileVersionId}/CheckResult/{checkResultId} > GET /api/core/fileversion/{fileVersionId}/CheckResult/{checkResultId} > FileVersionCheckResultResource fields
text:
- `id`: Identifier for this check result.
- `fileVersionId`: File version identifier for this check result.
- `checkId`: Check identifier for this check result.
- `description`: Summary the user sees first, e.g. "Three issues were found". Best practice: immediately after starting an external check, create a result with outcome "info" and a description like "In Progress" so the user knows the request was received; when the check completes, PUT that same result with the final outcome and description, rather than creating a new one.
- `outcome`: Outcome of this check result: pass, fail, warning, or info. If left unset, it is derived from this result's findings: 0 findings -> no badge shown; 1+ fail -> red badge (count of fail+warn); 1+ warn, 0 fail -> orange badge (count of warnings); 1+ pass, 0 fail/warn -> green badge (count of passes); 1+ info, 0 fail/warn/pass -> gray "Info" badge. Setting outcome explicitly overrides this rollup.
- `createdById`: ID of the user who created this check result.
- `createdOn`: Creation datetime in UTC time.
- `_links`: Hypermedia links (HAL-style) to related resources.
- `_embedded`: Hypermedia-embedded (HAL-style) related resources, inlined here when requested/expanded.

text:
Reading a maintenance job without embedded targets

In case of **hal+json**, all subresources (targets) are represented as links to these resources.

In case of **json**, all subresources (targets) are returned as null values.

```http
GET /maintenancejob/b6d2400e-ffce-489b-9e08-7324c9378206
accept: application/hal+json
```

```http
GET /maintenancejob/b6d2400e-ffce-489b-9e08-7324c9378206
accept: application/json
```

Reading a maintenance job with embedded targets

The **select-maintenancejob: targets** header embeds the targets collection directly in the response instead of just linking to it.

```http
GET /maintenancejob/b6d2400e-ffce-489b-9e08-7324c9378206
accept: application/hal+json
select-maintenancejob: targets
```

title: DAM API: PUT /record/{recordId} > PUT /api/core/record/{recordId} > Examples
text:
Immediate propagation for record updates

For POST, PUT and DELETE operations on the /record resource you can force an immediate update of the search index, or immediate propagation. To do so, add the boolean header/query-string parameter **set-immediateSearchIndexUpdate** and set it to "true". If you don't specify this parameter, or set it to "false", the change will be added to the queue of the Enterprise search synchronization process. Setting the parameter to true will immediately push the record changes to the search index, so that this record can immediately be found, e.g. while an ETL import is still running. This is important, for example, when importing both the child and parent of linked records.

Editing a record (full body)

"id" for addOrUpdate of a file version, additional file or file preview can be a token or a guid. When adding a new file version, additional file or file preview, you pass the token which you get after uploading a file (please check the "See also" section below). When editing, you pass the guid of an existing file.

To create a new file, you have to specify at least one file version with a token for its file content.

The client id must match the accessCode in the .validationAndRuleDisablingRules system setting, and that setting entry's "disableValidation" and/or "disableRules" must also be set to true.

```http
disable-validations: true
disable-rules: true
client-id: {clientId}
```

title: DAM API: PUT /record/{recordId} > PUT /api/core/record/{recordId} > Parameters
text:
- `recordId` (path, required): id of the record
- `API-VERSION` (header, required): The REST API version to target, e.g. "1".
- `Accept` (header, required): The desired response media type. If omitted, the server defaults to "application/hal+json", which includes "_links"/"_embedded" hypermedia so a client can navigate to related resources without constructing URLs itself. For most integrations, requesting "application/json" instead is simpler and produces a smaller, flatter response - recommended unless you need that hypermedia.
- `Authorization` (header, required): The bearer token used to authenticate the request.
- `User-Agent` (header, required): Identifies the calling application.
- `set-immediateSearchIndexUpdate` (header): When true, updates the search index immediately instead of waiting for the next scheduled update. This makes the change searchable sooner but slows down the request, since it now waits on indexing instead of returning as soon as the record is saved.
- `disable-validations` (header): When set, skips field and business rule validations.
- `disable-rules` (header): When set, skips rule execution for this operation.
- `client-id` (header): Client-supplied identifier used to correlate this request.
- `copyFromLatestVersion` (header): When set, only the latest file version is processed instead of all versions.
- `recreateAutomaticPreviews` (header): When set, recreates automatic previews for the record's files.
- `copyFilesInBackgroundProcess` (header): When set, copies files in a background process instead of synchronously.

title: DAM API: POST /record/bulkedits > POST /api/core/record/bulkedits
text:
Initiates edit record sessions in bulk

Initiates edit record sessions in bulk. This is the first step of the bulk edit session lifecycle: it opens an edit session for each record without persisting any changes, and returns a "token" field per record in the response. Pass those tokens back to PATCH /record/bulkedits to apply partial changes while keeping the sessions open, to PUT /record/bulkedits to commit and close them, or to DELETE /record/bulkedits to discard them.

Applies the sent changes to the editable records and saves them

title: DAM API: POST /records/edits > POST /api/core/records/edits > Examples
text:
Duplicating a record as draft

If header makeFileNamesUnique is set to True, then all file version file names will be updated - Copy {index} will be added to make file names unique across system, i.e. original Copy, original Copy 1, original Copy 2 and so on. If header makeFileNamesUnique is set to False (default value), then all file version file names will be same as in original record. If header usePreviewsFromSource is set to True, then for created in-memory duplicate record, we will update URI's for all Previews\Thumbnails\Additional Files to its matching pairs from original record. You can also specify the copyRelationshipField header which allows to relate original record and the copy via record link field with OneParentManyChildren Link Type. In the copy the original record will be set as parent in that field.

```http
POST /records/edits

copyFrom: 41f8115dd9714b27b5d8b7f1c1285d07
makeFileNamesUnique: true
usePreviewsFromSource: true
copyRelationshipField: Name of Record Link Field
```

title: DAM API: GET /record/{objectId}/trail > GET /api/core/record/{objectId}/trail > Examples
text:
Reading the audit trail of a record (This route only supports paging type: Skip, Take)

The 'filter' parameter is optional and has three valid values. If a different value is passed in the request, the DAM REST API will process the request as if no filter was passed. Valid values:
- "" (empty, no filter is applied)
- "change" (only record changes are returned)
- "download" (only downloads of files of the record are returned)

See the `Reading the audit trail of a record (This route only supports paging type: Skip, Take) (json)`, `Reading the audit trail of a record (This route only supports paging type: Skip, Take) (json 2)` and `Reading the audit trail of a record (This route only supports paging type: Skip, Take) (json 3)` response examples in the responses panel.

accept: application/hal+json
```

accept: application/hal+json
```

title: DAM API: POST /search/records > POST /api/core/search/records > Examples
text:
Advanced searching for records

For more complex search queries than the `filter` parameter supports, use this endpoint. The `facets` array lets you compute aggregated counts alongside the search results - see the request/response schemas for the full set of supported facet types and their parameters.

**Some remarks:**

- Due to the way search works, the returned `totalCount` is an approximation and might not be the same as the number of returned search results. The retrieved facet count is also an approximation.
- Facet values with a count of 0 are omitted from the reply, even if they are directly specified, e.g. as explicit values. If the consuming application needs to display facet values with a count of 0, it should keep track of them internally.
- The number of facets that can be returned per request is limited to 12. If more than 12 facets are submitted, the list is truncated - the search engine only includes the first 12, and the ignored facet names are listed in the response's `truncatedFacets` property.

title: DAM API: POST /search/records/ids > POST /api/core/search/records/ids > Examples
text:
Searching for record IDs

Takes the same request as `POST /search/records` and runs the same search, but returns only the IDs of the matching records instead of the records themselves.

**Some remarks:**

- The IDs come straight from the search index, in search order. They can include records that were deleted, or whose security changed, but that have not been re-indexed yet.
- Paging (`page`/`pageSize`, `skip`/`take`, `cursor`), sorting, facets, `truncatedFacets`, and the page size limits are the same as for `POST /search/records`. A page that exceeds the limit is silently shortened; advance by the number of IDs returned.
- `nextCursor` is returned only when the page is full, and is null otherwise.

title: DAM API: GET /setting/{settingName} > GET /api/core/setting/{settingName} > Examples
text:
Reading a setting

If the setting is found, a resource is returned containing the name and the value of the setting.

If the setting was not found, the API call will fail with a **404 Not found** HTTP status code.

```http
GET /setting/.defaultRecordTitleField
```

Reading a setting from a specific scope

If the setting is found, within a given scope, a resource is returned containing the name and the value of the setting.

If the setting was not found, the API call will fail with a **404 Not found** HTTP status code.

To access a setting through the Rest API, you must have the **Role required to change** which is defined on the setting definition.

```http
GET /setting/.defaultRecordTitleField?scope=usergroup&scopeId=d4889b57-af11-4da9-aba1-c96d1b6a22ec
```

title: DAM API: GET /settings > GET /api/core/settings > Examples
text:
Getting multiple settings

Use the "**names**" query parameter to specify a comma-separated list of setting names.

For example:

This request will not fail for the cases when a single setting fetch will:
- When a setting is not found: the missing setting will be omitted from the response.
- When a setting is not whitelisted and the user is not in the ADAM Administrator user group: it will not be returned either.
- When the user doesn't have the Role required to change: the aggregated value for the current requestor will be returned using the ADAM setting value fallback mechanism.
- When a setting is a **Role Setting**: it will not be returned in the response.
- If, due to all the specifics above, none of requested settings is returned, the response will simply be an empty collection (but not 404 not found).

```http
GET /settings?names=.recordFieldViewList,.userFieldViewList
Accept: application/hal+json
```

title: DAM API: GET /shareddownloadlinks > GET /api/core/shareddownloadlinks
text: Read a paged collection of shared download links

title: DAM API: GET /shareddownloadlinks > GET /api/core/shareddownloadlinks > Examples
text:
Listing shared download links

By default the collection only contains the shared download links created by the current user. The parameters are specified as http headers.

```http
GET /shareddownloadlinks
accept: application/hal+json
filter: expiresOn >= '2026-08-01'
sort: createdon desc
page: 1
pageSize: 25
```

Listing shared download links of all users

Members of the Administrators user group can list the links of all users of the tenant by adding the allUsers query string parameter. For any other user this returns 403 Forbidden.

```http
GET /shareddownloadlinks?allUsers=true
accept: application/hal+json
```

Filtering shared download links by file name

The collection can be filtered by link id, expiration date, revocation state, creator and file name, for example:

```http
GET /shareddownloadlinks?filter=File.FileName+%3D+'*brochure*'
accept: application/hal+json
```

Filtering shared download links by revocation and expiration

The boolean revoked field matches links that have (or have not) been revoked; combine it with an expiration date predicate to select only active links:

```http
GET /shareddownloadlinks?filter=expiresOn+%3E%3D+'2026-08-01'+and+revoked+%3D+false
accept: application/hal+json
```

GET /translations
accept: application/hal+json
filter: ModifiedOn in today

GET /translations?page=1&pagesize=10
filter: ModifiedOn in today
sort: createdon
